national_indicator_definition: The circular material use rate, also known as the circularity rate, measures the share of material recycled and fed back into the economy in overall material use. It shows the extent to which secondary raw materials replace primary raw materials, thereby reducing the need for the extraction of natural resources. It is calculated as the ratio of circular use of materials to overall material use.
national_rationale: The value of the indicator for Bosnia and Herzegovina for 2022 (2.2%) was calculated within the IPA MBP 2022 project – Statistical Project (SP) 5.6: Waste Statistics, using the Eurostat methodological approach. Circular use of materials is estimated on the basis of the amount of waste recycled in domestic recovery facilities, adjusted for imports and exports of waste intended for recovery. Overall material use comprises domestic material consumption and circular use of materials. Progress for this indicator cannot be calculated due to the lack of an adequate time series.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers overall material use in the economy and measures the contribution of recycled materials to the substitution of primary raw materials. The methodology is based on the Eurostat definition and calculation approach. For Bosnia and Herzegovina, a value for 2022 is available, calculated within the IPA MBP 2022 project – SP 5.6: Waste Statistics. Comparisons with other countries should take into account the coverage and completeness of waste treatment data, as well as the availability of data on material flows.
national_long_objective: Increasing the circular use of materials is an important prerequisite for more efficient use of natural resources and the transition from a linear to a circular economy. Among the objectives related to the circular economy in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Voluntary National Review on the implementation of the 2030 Agenda identifies the reuse of at least 30% of industrial waste as secondary raw materials, as well as a 30% increase, compared with 2020, in domestic production and use of recyclable products and products with a higher content of recycled materials. These objectives contribute to the development of the circular economy but do not represent a specific target value for the circular material use rate. No specific national target expressed as a percentage of overall material use has been established for this indicator.
eu_indicator_definition: The circular material use rate, also known as the circularity rate, measures the share of material recycled and fed back into the economy in overall material use. It is calculated as the ratio of circular use of materials to overall material use. A higher value indicates that a larger share of secondary raw materials is used as a substitute for primary raw materials, thereby reducing the need for the extraction of natural resources.
eu_rationale: The indicator is produced in accordance with the quality standards of European statistics. The data source is the European Statistical System (ESS), and the original Eurostat dataset is ENV_AC_CUR. Eurostat disseminates the indicator on the basis of data provided by countries. Circular use of materials is estimated on the basis of the amount of waste recycled in domestic recovery facilities, adjusted for imports and exports of waste intended for recovery. Overall material use is calculated as the sum of domestic material consumption (DMC) and circular use of materials. The indicator is updated annually.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers overall material use in the economy and makes it possible to monitor the contribution of recycled materials to reducing the consumption of primary raw materials. Data are collected annually and allow comparisons between EU Member States. The time series for the EU aggregate starts in 2004, while data for Member States and individual material categories are available from 2010 onwards.
eu_long_objective: In March 2020, the European Commission adopted the new Circular Economy Action Plan (CEAP), which aims to reduce pressure on natural resources and accelerate the transition to a circular economy. The plan covers the entire life cycle of products, from design and production to consumption and waste management, with a particular focus on waste prevention, reuse and material recycling. The 8th Environment Action Programme, adopted in 2022, further emphasises the transition towards a climate-neutral, resource-efficient and regenerative economy. Within the EU Sustainable Development Goals framework, the target is to double the circular material use rate by 2030 compared with 2020.
